name: maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_SelectMemberGauge
summary: Second entry point into the party-panel member-gauge selection: it first runs the window constructor 0x00325500 (the same ctor used by Menu_TalkParty_CreatePanel) and then falls through into the shared 31-member scan that binds the selected entry to the HP gauge window.
evidence: New context: the extra first call is the window ctor 0x00325500, whose other caller is Menu_TalkParty_CreatePanel, so this entry is 'construct the panel then select the gauge'. It has no direct callers and the two bodies merge, so the exact trigger is still unproven and the maybe_ name stays.

name: Ui_PartyPanel_SelectMemberGaugeByIndex
summary: Scans the 31 party ids and, for the entry whose ordinal matches the panel's requested slot (self->f_28 plus the base offset), rebinds the HP gauge window to that member and records it in f_74; otherwise keeps the gauge on the first visible member.
evidence: The body is entirely visible and every callee is now named: Party_EntryMatchesSelectedId, Battle_HpGaugeWindow_SetMember, Battle_HpGaugeWindow_DrawGauges, Game_GetDataManager. Its only named caller Ui_PartyPanel_BuildReserveRowsB uses it to point the gauge at the row being built, which fixes the 'select gauge by index' reading.

name: Battle_HpGaugeWindow_ShowDamageMask
signature: void Battle_HpGaugeWindow_ShowDamageMask(BattleHpGaugeWindow* self, int damage, u32 mask)
summary: Applies the pending damage/heal mask to the HP gauge: hides panes 3/4/5 or shows pane 5 with one of four fixed delta texts (2=heal-ish, 4=damage, 8=MP, 0x10=other) selected through Ui_Element_SetFlagBit0 / Ui_TextElement_SetString. Nothing is tweened here.
evidence: Body fully visible and its only caller is Battle_HpGaugeWindow_SetMember. It only flips pane visibility and writes one of four hard-coded text ids, so the old 'AnimateGauges' was misleading; the mask bits and the four text ids are literal, which supports 'show the damage mask' rather than an animation.

name: Ui_ReleaseSubObjectB
summary: Releases the sub-object referenced by slot word [1] through the UI core heap and clears the slot, returning the slot for chaining; a template copy of Ui_ReleaseSubObject (0x003BC520).
evidence: Byte-for-byte the same body as the confirmed Ui_ReleaseSubObject (0x003BC520), and its callers are generic teardown paths (Gfx_Resources_Release, Gfx_Resource_Recreate34, Ui_Screen_ReleaseMembers), not title-message code. The old 'Ui_TitleMessage_ReleaseChild' attributed the slot to a class the body never touches; the 'B' suffix marks the template copy.

name: Field_Gimmick_ActivateComponent1D8
signature: void Field_Gimmick_ActivateComponent1D8(void* controller, const void* params, float paramS0)
summary: Initialises the embedded gimmick sub-component at controller+0x1D8 from the caller's parameter block (forwarded in r1..r3/s0 to 0x0028981C) and stores controller+0x1D8 in controller->f_12C as the active sub-component.
evidence: Fourth of the six adjacent sub-component activators (0x3D55BC/+0x168, 0x3D55D8/+0x134, 0x3D55F4/+0x1A0, 0x3D5610/+0x1D8, 0x3D562C/+0x210, 0x3D5648/+0x224); all four callers are now confidently named Field_Gimmick update/event functions, which fixes both the subsystem and the 'activate component' action.

name: Ui_LayoutElement_DtorB
summary: Destructor body of the second UI layout-element class (vtable 0x00769ED8): releases its layout reference through Ui_LayoutRef_Release, detaches the cached resource, clears the back-pointer and runs Ui_LayoutElement_Dtor on the base.
evidence: It installs vtable 0x00769ED8 (the vtable of the confirmed Ui_LayoutElement_Dtor sibling), clears the resource slot and ends by calling Ui_LayoutElement_Dtor, returning base-8. That is a destructor entry, not the 'layout-ref release' the old name claimed; the vtable sibling is the new evidence.

name: maybe_Ui_StatusParamWindow_DtorB
signature: void maybe_Ui_StatusParamWindow_DtorB(void* self, u32 arg2, int arg3)
summary: Damaged-decompile variant of the status/parameter window destructor: installs vtable 0x0076BB28, releases the two layout references and runs Ui_Object_DtorBase, but the object pointer is rebuilt from a shifted argument (arg3>>9>>8).
evidence: The Ghidra body is damaged (base pointer reconstructed from arg3>>9>>8, unreachable-block removal) so the decompilation is not trustworthy beyond the vtable 0x0076BB28 and the Ui_LayoutRef_Release / Ui_Object_DtorBase calls; kept at 0.3 per the damaged-body rule.

name: Ui_StatusParamWindow_SetVisibleWithAnimThunk
summary: Vtable slot (+0x1C) of the status/parameter window class (vtable 0x0076BB28): a pure forwarding thunk that passes the caller's pane arguments straight to Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim.
evidence: The body is a single tail call to the now-named Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim and the slot belongs to vtable 0x0076BB28, whose other slots are the named Ui_StatusParamWindow_Ctor/Dtor/SetTreeState. The 'does not return' warning is the known Ghidra tail-call artifact.

name: Ui_EntrySet_AddByteE5
summary: Appends a node of kind 0xE5 carrying one byte value to an intrusive sorted entry list: allocates a 0x14-byte node with vtable 0x0075A554, links it and re-sorts; 0xFF means 'no value' and adds nothing.
evidence: Body fully visible; its callers are the now-named Menu_ProcessEntryQueue and Item_OnAcquired, and the set is reached through the UI object at +0x10 -> +0xA4, so it is a UI entry-set append of a byte command. The node kind 0xE5 and the 0xFF sentinel are literal.

name: Ui_Casino_DestroyFixedArrays
summary: Destroys the two fixed arrays of seven 0x50-byte elements at +0xC and +0x23C with std_destroy_range and element destructor 0x0032686C, then returns the object base; the accompanying constructor is Container_ArrayCtor (0x004066DC).
evidence: std_destroy_range is the confirmed array-destructor helper (0.80) and 0x0032686C is the element destructor, so 'Init' in the old name was backwards; every named caller (Ui_PokerTable_Dtor, Ui_RouletteWindow_DeletingDtor, Casino_Slot_Dtor, Ui_SlotWindow_Ctor cleanup path) is a casino window class, hence the casino prefix.

name: maybe_Casino_Poker_RotateHandSlots
summary: Reorders the dealt poker hand: shuffles the two ten-slot halves, swaps that many 2-byte slots between the halves and shuffles the first half again. The swap count comes from a game-RNG roll whose result Ghidra lost (extraout_r1).
evidence: All nine callers are the Casino_Poker_DealHand* variants and the three Casino_Poker_ShuffleU16 calls are named, so the poker reordering is certain. The loop bound is the lost register extraout_r1 (the RNG modulo result), so the exact reordering rule cannot be verified and the maybe_ stays.

name: Ui_ListWidget_ResetToFirstEntry
summary: Resets a list widget to its first entry: re-initialises the embedded item iterator at +0x74, points the widget at it, calls the widget virtual +0x5C and updates the selection pane through 0x001A6680 (row 0, cursor-bearing pane 0x1E).
evidence: Two named callers (Ui_SmithMenu_HandleListCommand, Ui_SmithMenu_HandleSortInput) use it after rebuilding/re-sorting the list, and the body re-inits ItemList_Iterator_Init and selects row 0. No scroll offset is touched anywhere, so the old 'ResetScroll' was a wrong noun.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_WrapRowB
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListWindow_WrapRowB(void* self, int delta, u32 arg3, int pageCount)
summary: Second cursor-row wrap variant: adds delta to the list row index (+0x4C), fetches the entry count through vtable+0x64 and wraps a negative row back into range. The upper clamp is lost to the truncated Thumb decode.
evidence: Same shape as the sibling 0x006E51E4 (maybe_Ui_ListWindow_WrapRow): delta on self[0x13] (=+0x4C), count via vtable+0x64, negative wrap. Only the division constant differs; three halt_baddata truncations mean the delta==0 case and upper clamp are unknown, so the name is aligned to the sibling but stays maybe_.

name: Field_SceneObject_SpawnItemFieldEffect
summary: If the scene object's item (+0x298) has kind 0x25 ('%'), creates the item's 2D field effect at the object's tile (f_78*8+8, f_7C*8) through Gfx_Effect2D_CreateSlot.
evidence: The body looks the item up with Item_LookupRecord, tests the item kind byte +0x0C against 0x25 and spawns the 2D effect at the tile; callers are the scene-object ctors/reset and GimmickItemEffectStart. The old '...IfItemRecord' read like a record check rather than the item's field-effect spawn, so the wording is fixed.

name: Field_SceneObject_SpawnItemFieldEffectB
summary: Template copy of Field_SceneObject_SpawnItemFieldEffect (0x0044C5C8): item kind 0x25 -> 2D effect at the object's tile. The item id passed to Item_LookupRecord was dropped by the decompiler in this copy.
evidence: Same body as 0x0044C5C8 (the only difference is the missing Item_LookupRecord argument in the decompilation) and its single caller is the named Field_SceneObject_CreateVariantEffects; the 'B' suffix marks the second template copy.

name: Ui_WindowPart_SetTextWithSe
summary: Sets a window-part text like Ui_WindowPart_SetText (0x0044FFC0) but appends control code 0x13, triggers the one-shot vtable+0x7C path guarded by f_34d, binds the string to the slot and queues sound effect 0x0B (handle kept in f_224).
evidence: The three-step tail is byte-for-byte the confirmed Ui_WindowPart_SetText family (std_String_AppendChar, one-shot vt+0x7C, Ui_Slot_BindControl) with control code 0x13 instead of 0x16, plus Sound_CommandQueue_Push_2(sound, 0xB, 0). The old 'Recipe...' name was already dropped; what remains is the text-set-plus-SE action.

name: Gfx_Sprite_BuildFootprintRect
signature: void Gfx_Sprite_BuildFootprintRect(int* outRect4, const int* sizeXY, const int* baseXY)
summary: Builds a 4-int placement rectangle {w, h, baseX + 1 - w/2, baseY + 1 - h} from a sprite size pair and a base coordinate pair (usually *0x007BE2D4); callers are the field marker/sprite/mesh setup paths.
evidence: The callee disassembly proves 0x31A658 computes {1-w/2, 1-h} from sizeXY (Ghidra dropped its r1), and the four callers are all named sprite/marker creation functions (Field_Marker_SetupSpriteObject, Field_Object2D_InitSpriteActor, Gfx_ModelPart_InitDualMesh, Field_SceneObject_InitSymbolFromLayout). 'Footprint' is the placement quad, which matches the stored w/h plus centre offset.

name: maybe_Battle_Actor_ApplyFlag77
summary: Applies actor flag 0x77 and returns 1 when the actor is valid, not in state 0x11B, and either the party record's byte f_667 is set or the flag is already present; returns 0 and changes nothing otherwise.
evidence: The body always sets the flag via vtable+0xE4(0x77) before returning 1, so the read via vtable+0xE8 only guards the set (it is not a Has* predicate). Callers Battle_CalcElementalDamage and Battle_ApplyMonsterEffect place it in the monster-effect path, but what flag 0x77 and party byte f_667 mean is still unknown.

name: maybe_Battle_RollStatusProc
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_RollStatusProc(void* actor, void* target, int statusId)
summary: Rolls 1..100 on the battle RNG and compares it with a game-setting threshold (record f_144/f_145/f_146) selected by the actor value (10..12, 8 or 2); returns 1 when the roll passes. Target must be alive (f_10) with f_768==0 and the global at work+0x2771B set.
evidence: The roll is the named func_001CA474(&battle rng,1,100) and the thresholds come from the now-named Game_GetDataManager settings record; caller Battle_ApplyDamageClamp and maybe_Battle_RollActionStatusChance support a status-proc reading. The actor codes and threshold fields are still undocumented, so the maybe_ stays at 0.45.

name: Party_Member_GetAttackCount
summary: Returns the member's number of attack instances: 2 when the equipped slot-0 item kind is 0x11 (falcon, two hits) or the member has an off-hand weapon, otherwise 1.
evidence: The body uses the established func_0035EB98 (party member) + func_006292F0(member,0) (slot-0 item) and the named Party_Member_HasOffhandWeapon, and treats item kind 0x11 (the FACTS falcon 2-hit subtype) exactly like an off-hand weapon. Callers use the result as a loop count in Battle_Message_BuildActorRowBig (0 < local_ac; i < local_ac) and in AI action evaluation, so it is an attack/row count, not an 'equipment category'.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_BuildSlotIds
summary: Large gimmick slot-setup routine (1408 bytes): the only recoverable statement is a std_ConstructArray of eight 4-byte entries at a 108-byte stack frame with constructor 0x006F0974; the stores that would show what ids are built were lost.
evidence: Ghidra ends the body at the std_ConstructArray call (the rest of the 1408-byte function is unreachable in the decompilation), so only the array-of-eight construction is verified. All three callers are now named gimmick slot/config functions (Field_Gimmick_BuildPartSlots, ApplyConfigBlock, InitSlotIds), which supports the subsystem but not a sharper name.

name: maybe_Field2D_Object_ApplyAttribute
signature: void maybe_Field2D_Object_ApplyAttribute(u32 ignored, u32 id, u32 arg3, u32 manager)
summary: Resolves the 2D scene object with the given id through the shared scene-sprite context and applies attribute constant 0xC41 to its model part at +0x3C.
evidence: The id lookup (func_002E5A34), Gfx_GetSceneSpriteContext and the model-part attribute call with literal 0xC41 are clear, and the named callers Field2D_Actor_StepMoveTargets / Field2D_Scene_RenderObjects fix the 2D object subsystem. What attribute 0xC41 means is unknown, so the maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Node_ComputeAttachedTransform
signature: void maybe_Node_ComputeAttachedTransform(float* out, void* node, float* params)
summary: Computes the transform of an object attached to a scene node: copies the parameter point, rotates the node basis (Math_TransformOffsetPoint), probes along the result with Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesAlongLine and writes the entry-relative position plus its base translation.
evidence: The copy/rotate/cast/store sequence is fully visible and the callees are named (Math_TransformOffsetPoint, Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesAlongLine); its callers are Field_SpinAction_Update and maybe_Battle_UpdateSkullRunAnchor, both field-action paths. The owning class and the two node offset groups (f_284..f_29C) remain unproven, so it stays maybe_.

name: Gfx_SceneSprite_Dtor
summary: Base destructor of the scene-sprite class with vtable 0x0077B0C0: installs the class vtable, releases the sprite child handle at +0x20 through the scene context and erases the embedded +0x4 red-black-tree node when the +0x14 flag is set.
evidence: Disassembly confirms the vtable store (0x0077B0C0), the scene-context call with [r5,#0x20], the +0x14 flag test and the rb-tree erase, i.e. a destructor body. The sibling 0x004E4FC4 is called from the named Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable and both use Gfx_GetSceneSpriteContext, so the old 'Ui3D effect pair' prefix had no support.

name: Gfx_SceneSprite_DtorB
summary: Base destructor of the second scene-sprite class (vtable 0x0077B0D8): installs the class vtable, pushes the UV scene node at +0x8 through maybe_Gfx_SceneNode_SetUV and erases the +0x4 red-black-tree node when the +0x14 flag is set.
evidence: Same destructor shape as 0x004E4BA4 with vtable 0x0077B0D8 and the +0x8 UV node; the only named caller is Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable. Nothing in the body or the caller set is UI3D, so 'SetEffectPairText' (which never wrote a string) is replaced by the destructor role.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteObject_OnNotify
summary: Sprite-object notification hook: runs the base notify 0x00406CB0 and then re-applies the sprite's scene handle (self+0x48) to the current scene context.
evidence: The base-notify call and the scene apply are clear, and the callee 0x002E6828 is now known to be the shared scene setter, but the 0x00406xxx base family is still only generically named, so 'OnNotify' remains a class-slot reading rather than a verified vtable name.

name: maybe_Field_ModelObj_ReleaseSprite
summary: Field model-object teardown: runs the base slot 0x00406D64 and then passes the sprite instance handle f_50 to the scene helper 0x002E7B58 (the counterpart of Field_ModelObj_CreateSprite, which stores f_50 from Gfx_Scene_CreateOrAttachSpriteEntry).
evidence: The counterpart creator 0x004FABC0 is confidently named Field_ModelObj_CreateSprite and its three callers are exactly the same three functions that call this one; f_50 is the sprite handle it stores. 0x002E7B58 itself has no readable body/name, so 'release' versus 'detach' is not proven and the maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field_QueryFourPoints
signature: void maybe_Field_QueryFourPoints(void* owner, int* origin, int* offsets, u8* results, u8* hitBytes)
summary: Runs four one-unit scene probes at the given relative offsets, storing a boolean per probe and optionally the first byte of each hit object.
evidence: The loop of four over func_002E7288 with owner layer f_AC / params f_9C and f_5C is literal, but the optional hit-byte pointer is the lost register unaff_r6, so the write-back half is only partly recovered; kept maybe_ per the damaged-decompilation rule.

name: Ui_ScreenCtor_vt7792D0
summary: Constructor of the UI screen class with vtable 0x7792D0: runs Ui_Screen_CtorBase, installs the vtable, resets the state words at +0x125C (to -1) and +0x1260 (to 0) and calls FieldParty_ResetMemberSlot.
evidence: Both named callers (Field_ObjectFactory_Type1353, Field_ObjectFactory_Kind20) are object factories that build sibling screens, and the body is the standard Ui_Screen_CtorBase + vtable + state reset; the vtable address is the only certain class identity, so the name encodes exactly that.

name: Battle_Ui_FormatActorNameArg
summary: Formats the battle actor's display name for the message window: if self->f_214 is clear it builds the gimmick/status message text, otherwise it formats the party member name (member+0xCA) with the format at 0x007BFF8A; the result is written to message argument slot 2.
evidence: All four callers are now named battle-UI paths (Battle_Ui_Balloon_UpdateState, Ui_BattleTargetMarker_Manager_Update, UpdateCommandState, UpdateState), and the body resolves the member via func_0035EB98 and writes arg slot 2 through the message-arg helper. 'Model label' was the first pass's guess; the actual data is an actor/member name plus a gimmick text id.

name: maybe_Battle_Effect_SpawnFocusEffect
summary: Selects and spawns one of the two battle focus-point effects for the model: reads the 0..1 ratio from vtable getters +0x90/+0x94 (0x90 is HP per FACTS) and calls Battle_Effect_SpawnFocusPointB below 0.5, otherwise Battle_Effect_SpawnFocusPoint, gated by bits 0x10/0x20 at +0xF22.
evidence: The callee pair is used only by this function and its sibling 0x004E20BC, and both are the named FocusPoint effect spawners; the callers Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForMember/All put it in the battle UI path. The 0.5 ratio was previously read as an LOD size, but vt[+0x90] is HP (FACTS), so 'LOD by screen size' was unsupported; what the +0xF22 gate bits mean keeps it maybe_.

name: Ui_ScreenCtor_vt77C648
summary: Constructor of the UI screen class with vtable 0x77C648: runs Ui_Screen_CtorBase, installs the vtable, clears the four state words at +0x1260..+0x126C and the tail bytes, and calls FieldParty_ResetMemberSlot.
evidence: Same construction pattern as 0x004D3590 (Ui_Screen_CtorBase + vtable + FieldParty_ResetMemberSlot), with the two named object-factory callers; the vtable address is the only certain class identity, so the name states exactly that.

name: Svc_InitSharedState
summary: Initialises one shared-state object: sets up the two LightEvents at +0 and +8 (one-shot), locks their embedded light locks, links the object into the shared list at 0x007E7AA4 and acquires shared resource id 0x207 through the service command, panicking on failure.
evidence: The shared-state family is now confirmed by Svc_ReleaseSharedState (0x005042F8, 0.5) and the Svc_ObjectPool_InitA/B siblings; this is the matching init path called from Ui_PresentWindow_Ctor. The decompilation is damaged only in the two panic-call argument registers (unaff_r4/in_lr); the init sequence itself is intact, as the disassembly-level LightEvent/semaphore calls show, so the confidence is raised to 0.5.

name: Sound_Command_FreeQueued
summary: Drains the sound command queue: pops every queued node, releases it through 0x00548800 and pushes the node back onto the free ring at queue+0xB4.
evidence: All six callers are now named sound driver/stream/shutdown paths (Sound_Driver_Tick, Sound_Driver_TickWithProfiling, Sound_StreamThread_Main, Sound_System_Shutdown, voice-pool allocate, DMA dispatch), and the queue-drain + free-ring push is fully visible; the only unnamed part is the release helper itself.

name: Sound_GetSystemHeader
summary: Copies the first two words of the sound-system object into the caller's buffer (an 8-byte header getter); the 'does not return' note is a Ghidra artifact.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00517A38..0x00517A5C is push/mov r4,r0/bl 0x005177DC (Sound_GetSystem)/mov r1,r0/mov r0,r4/pop/ldm {r1,r2}/stm {r1,r2}/bx lr, exactly an 8-byte copy out of the system object. Its caller is the named Sound_Driver_TickWithProfiling.

name: Sound_WaveCache_LoadDecodedWithHeader
signature: u32 Sound_WaveCache_LoadDecodedWithHeader(SoundWaveCache* cache, u32 waveId, SoundAllocator* alloc)
summary: Second half of a decoded-wave load: reads the 0x2C-byte wave header, allocates the header plus the per-channel offset table, decodes the blocks, writes the 'CIWV' trailer, initialises the descriptor and registers the buffer in the cache.
evidence: Its only caller is the confident Sound_WaveCache_LoadDecoded (0.5) and every callee is now named (Sound_SeqParam_GetWaveRef, Sound_WaveCache_ReadBlocks, Sound_Wave_InitDescriptor); the header size, the channel-table loop and the trailer word are literal, so the 'decoded with header' split is what the code does.

name: Sound_WaveCache_PreloadGroup
signature: int Sound_WaveCache_PreloadGroup(SoundWaveCache* cache, int group, SoundAllocator* alloc)
summary: Preloads a whole wave group: validates the bank header, walks the group's {waveId, size} table and loads each wave raw or decoded, aborting on the first failure; returns 1 when the whole group is resident.
evidence: The callers are now named resource-preparation paths (LoadCutScene, Sound_SeqPlayer_PrepareBank, Sound_Track_PrepareResources) and all six callees are named Sound_* helpers; the group-table walk and the raw/decoded branch are literal.

name: Field2D_Sprite_InitFromRecord
summary: Initialises a 2D sprite from a spawn record: copies the ids/position/scale/colour words, marks the sprite active, optionally takes the name from the current field target and resolves the kind-2 object record. The only caller is Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable.
evidence: The body writes the whole sprite state (f_3c, f_45/f_46, f_4c..f_5c), so it is an initialiser rather than a small setter, and the caller plus the named Field2D_GetSpriteName / Field_Object_GetKind2Record callees fix the field-2D subsystem. Renamed from 'SetFromRecord' to say it initialises the sprite.

name: Ui_ObjectList_DestroySlotsAAlt
summary: Template copy of Ui_ObjectList_DestroySlotsA: releases both reference pairs and destroys the three 0xC0-byte sub-objects at +0x14 and the two at +0x254, returning the object.
evidence: Byte-identical layout and body to the confirmed Ui_ObjectList_DestroySlotsA (0x005D0B5C, 3+2 slots of 0xC0 at +0x14/+0x254), and the caller set is the field UI-gimmick ctor/dtor pair that uses it as a reusable release pass. The already-named Ui_ObjectList_DestroySlotsB (0x005D18E0) is a different class (vtable 0x783D04, 0x30-byte stride at +5/+0x95), so this copy takes the 'Alt' suffix rather than a duplicate B.

name: maybe_BattleScene_CountVisibleUnits
summary: Counts the visible entries of the battle unit list at battle+0x4254 through Container_List_CountVisible; the remainder of the body is lost to a bad-instruction truncation.
evidence: The only recoverable work is Container_List_CountVisible on the first battle unit list (+0x4254, per FACTS) and the body ends in halt_baddata, so only 'count visible units' is supported. The old 'UpdateScreenState2' invented a screen-state role; the count is at least literal in the code.

name: BattleScene_AssignUnitAnimSlot
signature: u8 BattleScene_AssignUnitAnimSlot(void* battle, int spriteIndex, int activeCount)
summary: Chooses an animation slot (0..3, 4 = none) for each of the four 2D unit sprites by inspecting the active battle units at battle+0x428C and their model variants, so sprites sharing an animation do not collide; returns the slot chosen for the requested sprite.
evidence: The body walks the battle unit lists at battle+0x428C, uses BattleScene_GetUnitModelVariant and the named caller BattleScene_UpdateUnitModelTransforms stores the return value as the child's +0x114 anim-track index. That fixes the subsystem as the battle scene, not a generic Gfx SceneSprite2D.

name: maybe_EntryTable_LookupHandle
signature: void* maybe_EntryTable_LookupHandle(void* table, const u8* desc)
summary: Searches the three 0x10-byte entries of the handle table at table+8 for one whose flag byte +0xC intersects desc[2] and whose handle passes func_0062AA7C; returns the selected handle word (entry+8 when desc[0]==1, else entry+4) or null.
evidence: The table walk and the desc[2] mask test are literal and the callers are now named camera/object/text paths (Camera_ApplyWorkEntries, Camera_UpdateWorkEntry, Camera_IsCandidateVisible, Object_MarkReleased, Text_LayoutRecord), which confirms it is a shared handle-slot lookup and that callers use the return value. What desc[0]/desc[1] select and which owner class the table belongs to is still open, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_BattleAi_CheckActionStatGate
signature: u32 maybe_BattleAi_CheckActionStatGate(void* self, void* actor, int actionId)
summary: AI stat gate for one action id: ids 0x1E/0x1F reject equipment of kind 0x14/0x0E and compare the member's attack value against Battle_GetMaxUnitMetric(self,3); ids 0x23/0x24 and 0x27/0x28 compare other actor stats (records f_136/f_138) against metrics 5 and 4; everything else passes.
evidence: Its only caller is BattleAi_PickCandidateByWeight and the callees are now named (Battle_GetMaxUnitMetric, func_006292F0 for the equipped item, func_0035EB98 for the member), so this is an AI candidate filter on a percentage-of-stat threshold; no equip/use call exists, so the old 'CanEquipOrUse' was an invented predicate. The meaning of the ids remains unknown.

name: BattleAi_SelectActionForMode
signature: u32 BattleAi_SelectActionForMode(u32 context, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, void* unit, u32 filter, int mode)
summary: Selects the AI candidate action for the unit's current action record: modes 0..2 dispatch on record kind 4/3/6 to the damage-target picker, FindBestCandidate or the weighted picker; modes 3..8 additionally require the record id 0x1E/0x1F, 0x27/0x28 or 0x23/0x24 before handing the candidate to the picker; returns 0 when nothing matches.
evidence: Its only caller is BattleAi_FilterUsableCandidates and every callee is a BattleAi_* helper (FindBestCandidate, PickCandidateByWeight, PickRandomTargetAboveDamage) plus Battle_GetMaxUnitMetric; the signature's unit record is the skill/spell table entry. The subsystem prefix was 'Battle_' but all the context is the AI evaluator, so it is renamed to BattleAi_.

name: maybe_Field2D_Layer_GetField12
summary: Returns byte +0x12 of the layer record at layer->f_04->f_298; the value is compared for equality across the 0x38-byte Field2D layer entries (collision, map build, layer update) and passed to the map-chip code in ResetWalkTrigger.
evidence: Disassembly ldr r0,[r0,#4]; ldr r0,[r0,#0x298]; ldrb r0,[r0,#0x12] is certain, and the four callers are now named Field2D layer/collision functions. Whether the byte is a layer id, a floor index or a tag is still ambiguous (the comparisons do not expose its origin), so the neutral field name is kept.

name: Field2D_Layer_GetKindGroup
summary: Maps the Field2D layer record's type byte (+0x13) to a coarse group: 1 for types 0/1/5, 2 for type 2, 3 for types 3/4/7, 0 otherwise; used by Field2D_Scene_UpdateLayers.
evidence: The switch is fully visible and its only caller is the named Field2D_Scene_UpdateLayers, which classifies layers for update; the function literally converts a layer kind into a group, so the name is exactly what the body does even though the group meanings are not labelled.

name: Field2D_MapChip_ResolvePositionAtOffset
signature: void Field2D_MapChip_ResolvePositionAtOffset(Field2DPosition* out, Field2DObject* obj, u32 offset)
summary: Maps an offset along a 2D map object's walk path to a world position: adds the per-offset pixel delta to the object origin, starts the chip walk, traces one ray step and transforms the result; writes chip id, step result and x/y to out, or zeroes it when the trace fails.
evidence: Its callers are the now-named Field2D_MapChip_QueryCollisionAt and Field2D_MapChip_FindReachablePath, and every callee is a named Field2D helper (BeginChipWalk, TraceRayStep, Actor_TransformPosition, PackLayerChipIds); the fill/zero branches are fully visible.

name: Gfx_Movie_GetReadyFrame
signature: u32 Gfx_Movie_GetReadyFrame(MovieStream* stream, u32 arg2, u32* out)
summary: Queries the movie stream's current frame source: returns 0 with the ready surface pointer in *out, or 0xE (not ready) with *out cleared; a null stream returns 1.
evidence: The four callers are the named movie-decoder pipeline functions (FeedVideo, FeedAudio, CheckEndOfStream, ReadTextSamples) and the body's state byte test plus 0xE return are literal; the only unnamed part is the MoLive getter, which does not affect the ready-frame role.

name: std_introsort_itemName4
signature: void std_introsort_itemName4(u32* first, u32* last, int depth)
summary: Introsort for 4-byte item-bag entries: the median-of-three pivot and partition compare entries through Item_CompareFieldKey16 (item sort key, raw u16 id as tie-breaker), and the depth-0 fallback builds a heap with std_push_heap_itemName4.
evidence: The callers are the named Item_SortEntryArrayBySortKey and ItemBag_SortEntriesBySortKey, the heap sibling is std_push_heap_itemName4 and the comparator Item_CompareFieldKey16 is named; the only damage is Ghidra's 'unreachable block' warnings in the tail. This is the CRT introsort instantiation for the 4-byte item entries, so the template-style name is appropriate.

name: Gfx_WaitForDisplayState5
summary: Waits for a display-state request to complete: waits for the GPU IPC channel to be idle, requests display state 5, then polls Gfx_IpcCmd190040(state), unlocking the scheduler and sleeping between polls until the result leaves the transient codes; maps 'already in requested state' (0xC8A0CFFC) to 0.
evidence: Its two callers are Engine_InitializeSubsystems and Gfx_UpdateDisplayStateB, and the callees are named GPU IPC helpers (Gfx_WaitForIpcIdle, Gfx_IpcCmd190040, Os_UnlockScheduler); the state-5 request and the three transient result codes are literal. This is a display-state wait, not the Svc_ role the first pass assumed.
